'''''Pilularia minuta''''' is a species of [[fern]] in the family [[Marsileaceae]]. It is an [[Ephemeral plant|ephemeral]] species that relies on seasonal flooding. Though widely distributed across the [[Mediterranean basin]], it is considered an [[endangered species]] due to [[habitat fragmentation]].

==Distribution and habitat==
''Pilularia minuta'' has a [[Population fragmentation|fragmented]] distribution across the Mediterranean basin and can be found in [[Algeria]], [[Croatia]], [[Cyprus]], [[France]] ([[mainland France]] and [[Corsica]]), [[Greece]] (east [[Aegean Islands]]), [[Italy]] ([[mainland Italy]], [[Sardinia]], and [[Sicily]]), [[Morocco]], [[Portugal]], [[Spain]] ([[mainland Spain]] and the [[Balearic Islands]]), [[Tunisia]], and [[Turkey]]. It grows in [[Vernal pool|temporary]] [[freshwater]] pools at low [[elevation]]s in a diverse range of habitats including forests, [[matorral]]s, and [[agricultural land]]s.<ref name=iucn/>

==Description==
''Pilularia minuta'' is a small and delicate fern. The creeping [[Plant stem|stem]] measures approximately {{cvt|4–6|cm}} long and {{cvt|0.5–0.7|mm}} in diameter. Each mature stem consists of twelve or more segments, with individual internodes measuring {{cvt|3–8|mm}} long. The nodes each bear a single leaf, one or two roots, and sometimes a new bud or branch. The roots are usually simple but may be branched. The upright, slender leaves measure {{cvt|35–40|mm}} long and {{cvt|0.5–0.7|mm}} in diameter. When fruiting, the [[Sporocarp (ferns)|sporocarp]], bearing a spherical capsule, arises from a stem node at the base of the leaf and is covered in tawny hairs. Mature sporocarps are borne on {{cvt|1.5–2.5|mm}} [[Peduncle (botany)|peduncles]].<ref name=Development>{{cite journal |last1=Johnson |first1=Duncan S. |year=1933 |title=Structure and Development of ''Pilularia minuta''. Durieu Manuscript |journal=[[Botanical Gazette]] |publisher=[[University of Chicago Press]] |volume=95 |issue=1 |pages=104–127 |doi=10.1086/334368 |jstor=2471218}}</ref><ref name=Hydro>{{cite journal |last1=Daoud-Bouattour |first1=Amina |last2=Bottollier-Curtet |first2=Marion |last3=Jamaa |first3=Hafawa Ferchichi-Ben |last4=Ghrabi-Gammar |first4=Zeineb |last5=Saad-Limam |first5=Samia Ben |last6=Rhazi |first6=Laïla |last7=Muller |first7=Serge D. |year=2014 |title=Effects of hydrology on recruitment of ''Pilularia minuta'' Durieu (Marsileaceae), an endangered plant of Mediterranean temporary pools |journal=Aquatic Botany |volume=112 |pages=76–83 |doi=10.1016/j.aquabot.2013.08.001|bibcode=2014AqBot.112...76D }}</ref>

==Ecology==
''Pilularia minuta'' is an amphibious [[annual plant]] with a short life cycle that  requires high light levels and grows only on non-[[calcareous]] substrates. Stems and leaves begin to develop in flooded conditions from late February to early March, with the plant drying out and dying between May and June. Sporocarps form after the leaves have matured, while the plant is still submerged, but only mature once the plant has dried out. The [[spore]]s are capable of surviving this dry period, but can only [[Germination|germinate]] when the substrate is completely saturated.<ref name=Hydro/>

==Conservation status==
''Pilularia minuta'' is listed as [[Endangered species (IUCN status)|endangered]] on the [[International Union for the Conservation of Nature]]'s [[Red List]] under criteria B2ab(i,ii,iii,iv,v), based on its small and fragmented area of occupancy. The population appears to be in decline as a result of [[habitat destruction]].<ref name=iucn/>

''P. minuta'' is protected in Europe under the [[Berne Convention on the Conservation of European Wildlife and Natural Habitats|Bern Convention]] and [[Ex situ conservation|conserved ''ex situ'']] by the [[Conservatoire botanique national méditerranéen de Porquerolles]] in [[Porquerolles]], France.<ref name=iucn/>
